predecessors.note: The KNU, founded 5 February 1947, declared member groups part of the state of Kawthoolei in October 1947 and 'declared formal war on the government' on 31 January 1949 (Kawthoolei page). The land is the researcher's reading of the 2017 claim.

capitals.name: Taungoo (provisional government)
capitals.note: May 1949: 'the KNU set up a provisional government in Taungoo'; the KNU 'launched a political campaign from their capital in Taungoo in May 1949'. The page does not say how long it stood, so the span ends with the year the page dates; Taungoo is in Bago Region, outside Kayin State, and the 1949 keyframe adds a 30 km Taungoo circle for that year. Coordinates from the gazetteer.

capitals.name: Papun (Hpapun), capital of the Kawthoolei Free State
capitals.note: 1953: the KNU 'announced the declaration of the Kawthoolei Free State, based in its capital, Papun'. The Hpapun page gave no coordinates, so Manerplaw's (which lies in Hpapun Township, Manerplaw page) stand in as a placeholder. The span to 1974 ends the year before Manerplaw was established. The span starts in 1950 because the Taungoo span now ends in 1949; 1950-1952 is a bridging judgment (page silent) and the Free State is declared 'based in its capital, Papun' only in 1953.

capitals.name: Manerplaw (Klo Yaw Lay)
capitals.note: Manerplaw 'was established in 1975' and was the KNU headquarters 'until 1995' (KNU infobox); the Manerplaw page gives 17.725 N, 97.735 E and no date for the KNU's move there. Captured 27 January 1995. The pages name no later headquarters.

After the 2021 coup KNU Brigade 5 overran a base near the Thai border (27 March 2021); the KNU page gives 'approximately 61% of Karen State' (15 July 2025) and no map. The drawn shape is the 1995-2020 one through 2023 and the true hold is wider on some sides; the 2024 gains at Hpapun and Manerplaw are events and the 2024 keyframe.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Two gains in 2024 return the Manerplaw pocket to the KNU: the KNLA 'claimed to have seized' Hpapun on 28 March 2024 (Hpapun page) and the KNU and KNLA 'recaptured' Manerplaw on 17 December 2024 (Manerplaw page), so the 1995 loss is undone and Kayin State is drawn whole, as in 1949-1994. This overstates the ground held: the KNU page gives 'approximately 61% of Karen State' on 15 July 2025, so the whole of Kayin drawn here is wider than the page's share, as the earlier keyframes are. Soft.

The pages give the claimed Kawthoolei, not a held boundary.

ledger.note: 1950: the Taungoo country passes back to the government (bridging judgment, page silent). The Kawthoolei page says the KNU lost at the Battle of Insein and does not say how long the Taungoo government lasted or what happened to Taungoo afterwards; the loss is placed in 1950 so that the 1949 keyframe agrees with the 1950 one.

1953: the KNU 'announced the declaration of the Kawthoolei Free State, based in its capital, Papun'. The capitals list moves the KNU from Taungoo (1949) to Papun from 1950; 1950-1952 is a bridging span and the page names Papun as capital only at this 1953 declaration.

1975: Manerplaw is established; 'Manerplaw was established in 1975' (Manerplaw page) and the KNU headquarters is there 'until 1995' (KNU infobox). The year is the page's; that the KNU headquarters moved there in 1975 itself is the researcher's reading, so confidence 2.

notes: Rebel state added by se-04-x (the union-of-burma dossier lists the KNU as a counterpart needing a dossier). No page gives KNU-held ground for any year before July 2025, so Kayin State (the claimed Kawthoolei core) is a stand-in; the KNU page's 61 percent of Karen State (15 July 2025) is outside the 2024 end year. The 7 January 2026 proclamation of a 'Republic of Kawthoolei' by the Kawthoolei Army (KTLA) is disowned by the KNU ('controls no territory') and is not drawn. Gaps: no capital after 1995 on any page; Papun's coordinates; the seven KNU districts are not named on the KNU page. The 1964 Ne Win offer to retitle Kayin State as Kawthoolei is on the Kawthoolei page without a map effect. Kayin admin1 excludes the Taungoo hills (Bago Region). The Mon (New Mon State Party), Karenni (KNPP), Pa-O, Kachin and Arakan armies are separate insurgent zones (kachin-independence-organization is written here; the others are counterparts_needing_dossiers). The contest reopened in March 2021 stays open at the dossier's end (2024). Page budget: 5 pages. Repair pass 2026-10-25: (1) the two 2024 gains are in the ledger and the dossier has a 2024 keyframe of the whole of Kayin (Hpapun 2024-03 at confidence 2 because the page says 'claimed'; Manerplaw 2024-12-17 at confidence 3). The Hpapun circle is at the township coordinates because no page prints the town's, and the Manerplaw gain subtracts it. The old note that 'Manerplaw/Hpapun' were one circle was wrong in that the two places are about 35 km apart. (2) Capital: Taungoo now ends in 1949, the one year the page dates; the 1949 keyframe adds a 30 km Taungoo circle and the ledger has a 1949-05 gain and an undated 1950 loss (confidence 1, page silent); Papun starts in 1950 as a bridging span. The Insein stand of 1949 is on the Kawthoolei page only as a defeat ('the KNU lost at the Battle of Insein') with no detail, so no Insein circle is drawn. (3) The 1975 move to Manerplaw is now confidence 2. Thin items left: no page dates any shrinking of KNU ground between the 1970s and 1995, and none maps the seven districts.
